rv.q: Cruise is not just a play, it is a slice of history.
One year on, with life returned largely to normal, that raw resonant power remains intact, the play an enduring life affirming tribute to a vanished queer history.
I honestly cannot state how much Cruise blew me away and I don’t think there are enough superlatives to express my thoughts on it.
Holden has written one of the great plays of the last year so don’t miss this second chance to go cruising.

Here, under Bronagh Lagan’s taut direction, this one-man stage contribution to that canon, more than earns its place and provides an evening of joyous spectacle, sexy, frivolous asides, relatable characters and moving poignancy on the journey.
They have taken something that was already pretty special and turned it into an absolute masterpiece.

Holden and his outstanding team have crafted a story that finds joy, humanity, and life set in such a time of darkness, and as I dry my tear-stained cheeks I thank them from the very bottom of my heart.
It’s one the easiest five stars for a show I’ve seen this year and I truly hope we get to see more of it.
Cruise is one of the most engaging, emotional and life-affirming shows you will see this year.
Holden’s play is as much a dizzying dash back as it is a hopeful look and drive forwards.
Jack Holden's incredible one-man show is a blistering ode to the AIDS crisis, told in a spectacularly contemporary way

cn.t: Jack Holden's Olivier-nominated solo show about 1980s Soho and the AIDS crisis earns near-universal acclaim for its virtuoso performance, punchy writing, and euphoric yet poignant storytelling that's both a thrill ride and a masterclass.

vr.q: this is easily a five-star production of a five-star play for me
